sources.entry: flask-cors - A Flask extension for handling Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS).

summary.one_liner: flask-cors is a Flask extension that adds Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) headers to Flask routes so browsers can make cross-origin AJAX requests.
summary.what_it_does: The package provides a Flask extension that, by default, enables CORS on all routes for all origins and methods. Its CORS options can be set per resource by passing a dictionary that maps URL paths (such as /api/*) to option sets. A decorator named cross_origin can be placed under a Flask route to enable CORS on that single route instead. The README says cookies are not sent across domains by default, and that credentialed requests can be enabled through the documentation, with a reminder to add CSRF protection first. For troubleshooting, it describes turning on DEBUG logging for the flask_cors logger. The README does not list every option; it points to external documentation for the full set.
use_cases: Allow a browser frontend on another domain to call a Flask API
Enable CORS for all routes of a Flask app
Restrict CORS to an /api/* path prefix
Add CORS to a single Flask route with a decorator
Debug why cross-origin requests fail in a Flask app
notable: Enables CORS for all routes, origins and methods with one line by default
Per-resource option mapping using path patterns
Based on Armin Ronacher's HTTP Access Control decorator
Makefile targets with uv for development (make test)
caveats: Cookies are not sent cross-domain by default; enabling credentialed requests has security implications and needs CSRF protection
The README does not list all options inline; full reference is in external documentation
Designed around a simple all-domains philosophy, so fine-grained control requires per-resource configuration
